Priors for Bayesian fits

Source: R/bayes-priors.R
prior.Rd

Priors live on the coefficients of each linear predictor (on the link scale), on random effect standard deviations and on random effect correlations. A prior is written as a distribution call such as "normal(0, 2.5)"; the same specification is translated to 'Stan' and to the BUGS language used by 'JAGS' and 'OpenBUGS'.

Usage

prior(dist, par = NULL, class = c("b", "Intercept", "sd", "cor"), coef = NULL)

Arguments

dist

Prior distribution as a string.

par

Distribution parameter the prior applies to (NULL for all).

class

"b" (coefficients other than the intercept), "Intercept", "sd" or "cor".

coef

Optional coefficient name (for class = "b") or random effect term label (for "sd" and "cor").

Value

An object of class regcomp_prior; combine several with c().

Details

Supported prior distributions: normal(mean, sd), student_t(df, location, scale), cauchy(location, scale), logistic(location, scale), exponential(rate), gamma(shape, rate), uniform(lower, upper) and, for correlations, lkj(eta). Standard deviation priors are truncated to positive values.

Defaults: normal(0, 5) for intercepts and coefficients, student_t(3, 0, 2.5) for standard deviations and lkj(2) for correlations ('Stan'; BUGS engines use an inverse Wishart with identity scale for correlated random effects, which is noted in the fit).

Examples

p <- c(prior("normal(0, 1)", par = "mu", class = "b"),
       prior("student_t(3, 0, 1)", class = "sd"))
p
#> normal(0, 1)                 class b         par mu     coef (all)
#> student_t(3, 0, 1)           class sd        par (all)  coef (all)
